issuer: the New Hampshire Division of Motor Vehicles (Department of Safety)
note: The DMV's licensing fees page (read 2026-10-30) gives an operator licence (not federally compliant) at $50 ($60 REAL ID) and the youth operator licence at $10 a year up to 21, so the operator licence is held from 21 (a youth operator licence is had from 16, the FAQ says). Its term isn't stated on the pages read, so it is null; the Revised Statutes (gc.nh.gov) gave an empty reply from the server and weren't read. The first-licence page issues a non-driver ID to residents 12 and older without a licence, valid 5 years; the fee page gives it at $20.

sources.title: NH DMV, Licensing Fees
sources.said: Operator (not federally compliant) $50.00 ... Youth Operator $10.00 per year up to age 21 ... Non-Driver Identification Card $20.00

sources.title: NH DMV, FAQs
sources.said: At what age can I obtain a driver license? 16 years of age

sources.title: NH DMV, Apply for Your First Driver's License/Non-Driver ID
sources.said: An applicant must be a New Hampshire resident who is at least 12 years of age and who does not currently have a valid driver license. ... The permanent Non-Driver Identification card will be valid for 5 years.
